review_candidates.description: About the Job Altryon, Inc. is the data center development company of Cebron Financial Group, Inc. Altryon develops full-stack AI data center campuses integrated with dedicated behind-the-meter power generation. Our thesis is direct: the long-term economic value of AI deployment accrues to infrastructure owners. We develop, own, and operate campuses in markets where reliable firm power is scarce and AI-driven compute demand is accelerating, with development activity across Africa, India, Southeast Asia, Latin America, and North America. Africa is a priority development region. Our target markets include Nigeria, Kenya, South Africa, and Egypt, with additional markets across the continent evaluated on a selective basis. In these markets, data localization requirements, cloud expansion, and enterprise and government AI adoption are driving compute demand that grid infrastructure cannot reliably serve, and firm power commands a structural premium. Campuses are sized from 5 MW to 200 MW and delivered on a phased development basis. The Role We are seeking a Senior Vice President, Data Center Development – Africa, based in Johannesburg, Lagos, or Nairobi, to lead the origination and execution of our African development pipeline. Origination is the core of this mandate. Altryon's African platform will be only as strong as the sites and opportunities it controls, and you will be responsible for finding them. You will build and run a proprietary sourcing process across the continent: identifying campus sites, uncovering power-anchored opportunities that are not on the open market, and converting the strongest of them into controlled positions. From there, you will own the full pre-construction lifecycle through power path validation and interconnection feasibility, delivering fully de-risked, construction-ready projects. What You Will Do Site and Opportunity Origination –     Build and own a proprietary pipeline of campus sites and development opportunities across Nigeria, Kenya, South Africa, Egypt, and additional African markets, maintaining a continuously replenished funnel from initial identification through site control –     Lead country-level market screening, integrating demand signals, power sector conditions, regulatory posture, currency convertibility, and political risk into disciplined go/no-go recommendations that determine where origination effort is deployed –     Build and direct a network of land brokers, local counsel, surveyors, and site consultants in each target market to identify parcels with credible proximity to power interconnection, fiber routes, subsea cable landing stations, and end-market demand –     Originate opportunities beyond the open land market, including special economic zones and technology parks, industrial and logistics estates, brownfield and legacy power generation sites, and the landholdings of telecom operators, tower companies, and industrial groups –     Identify power-anchored opportunities where firm generation already exists or can be co-located, including independent power producers with uncontracted or stranded capacity, gas producers and processors with associated or flared gas, mining and industrial operators with captive generation, and renewable developers with expansion capacity –     Engage directly with private landowners, estate and zone operators, and generation owners to structure site access through options, conditional agreements, long-term leases, and joint development arrangements, with all engagement involving state-owned counterparties conducted through approved counsel –     Apply a consistent site scoring framework covering power path, interconnection, land and title, fiber, water and cooling, permitting, and demand proximity to rank opportunities and concentrate diligence spend on the highest-conviction sites –     Report pipeline status to Altryon leadership on a disciplined cadence, including stage-gate position, capital at risk, and expected conversion timeline for every opportunity Development Execution –     Assess power availability at each candidate site, including grid capacity, utility reliability and load-shedding exposure, tariff structures, and the feasibility of dedicated behind-the-meter and captive generation (gas, solar plus storage, geothermal, hybrid configurations) under each market's licensing regime –     Lead interconnection feasibility analysis, engaging national utilities, transmission operators, and regulators (Eskom, NTCSA, and NERSA in South Africa; TCN, NERC, and state electricity regulators in Nigeria; Kenya Power, KETRACO, and EPRA in Kenya; EETC and EgyptERA in Egypt) to validate interconnection pathways, timelines, and cost –     Secure site control through options and conditional agreements while running parallel diligence on title, land tenure, permitting, environmental and social clearance, and fiber connectivity –     Build and manage relationships with utilities, energy ministries, regulators, and permitting and investment promotion authorities, working through approved pan-African energy and projects counsel and Altryon's Strategic Advisory Council –     Coordinate with EPC partners and generation OEMs on constructability, delivery timelines, and cost benchmarks during pre-development –     Prepare projects for offtake engagement, ensuring every site presented to telcos, banks, governments, and enterprise customers carries a validated power path and delivery timeline –     Represent Altryon with development finance institutions and co-investment partners on project-level diligence What You Bring –     12+ years in power, energy, or digital infrastructure development in Africa, with direct experience taking projects from origination through site control and interconnection –     A proven origination record: a demonstrable history of personally sourcing, screening, and securing control of infrastructure sites and development opportunities, including off-market and negotiated transactions –     An established sourcing network of landowners, land brokers, zone and estate operators, generation owners, and local counsel in at least two major African markets –     Demonstrated expertise in grid interconnection processes, utility engagement, and power procurement in at least two African markets –     Deep familiarity with African power sector structures, including IPP frameworks, PPA negotiation and bankability, wheeling and open-access arrangements, eligible customer regimes, and embedded and captive generation licensing –     Hands-on experience with land and title diligence, land tenure structures, and permitting in complex jurisdictions –     Established relationships with utilities, regulators, energy ministries, or development finance institutions (AfDB, IFC, DFC, BII, Afreximbank, and Africa Finance Corporation ecosystem preferred) –     Working knowledge of IFC Performance Standards and DFI environmental and social diligence requirements –     Rigorous compliance posture, with direct experience operating under FCPA and UK Bribery Act standards –     Fluency in English required; French, Arabic, or Portuguese an advantage –     Based in or willing to relocate to Johannesburg, Lagos, or Nairobi, with regular travel across the continent Why This Role You will be a founding development leader for Altryon's African platform. Africa's installed data center capacity remains a small fraction of what its population, digital economy, and data localization requirements demand, while power availability, grid reliability, and permitting remain the binding constraints. That gap between compute demand and deliverable firm power is the opportunity, and it is exactly what Altryon's power-first model is built to close. You will be instrumental as to where Altryon builds, shape how proj for LinkedIn qualificationects are structured, and determine how the African platform scales. The laboratory of Javier Gordon Ogembo, Ph.D., at the Beckman Research Institute of City of Hope invites applications from highly motivated, creative, and exceptionally talented scientists for two postdoctoral scholar positions. Advance gamma-herpesvirus infection and vaccine development studies, including work focused on EBV, KSHV, and rhLCV. Support antibody discovery and immunotherapeutic research, including monoclonal and neutralizing antibody development. Investigate vaccine-induced humoral and cellular immunity, including antibody, B-cell, and T-cell responses. Use advanced in vivo models for vaccine and antibody testing, including conventional and humanized mice, transgenic models, rabbits, non-human primates, and patient-derived xenograft (PDX) models. Study viral pathogenesis, host-virus interactions, viral entry, and mechanisms of immune evasion. Conduct preclinical evaluation of vaccines and immunotherapies for infection and virus-associated cancers. Your qualifications should include: Ph.D., M.D., Ph.D./M.D., Ph.D./D.V.M., or equivalent doctoral degree, a strong record of peer-reviewed publications, and demonstrated ability to independently design, execute, and interpret research. The Opportunity Managing Director, Infrastructure Debt, Americas & APAC – New York, NY / Whippany, NJ MetLife Investment Management (“MIM”) is hiring a Managing Director to originate, source, and structure investment-grade and high-yield infrastructure transactions as part of the Infrastructure Debt, Americas & APAC team. The Managing Director will focus on driving disciplined growth through sourcing debt to support separate managed accounts, commingled funds, and structured vehicles aligned with client mandates. Leadership, Team Development & Platform Growth Build, lead, and mentor a high-performing origination and underwriting team; provide coaching, performance feedback, and career development support. Demonstrated track record of sourcing and executing infrastructure debt investments across the Americas (and ideally the APAC region).
